faq.q: What is the core difference between direct and regular mutual funds?
faq.a: The core difference lies in the expense ratio. Direct plans are purchased directly from the AMC and do not include distributor commissions, resulting in a lower expense ratio. Regular plans are bought through intermediaries and include these commissions, leading to a higher expense ratio.

faq.q: How does SEBI's new rule affect existing mutual fund investments?
faq.a: SEBI's new rule, effective November 1, 2026, makes direct plans the default option on AMC digital platforms for *new* investments. It does not automatically convert your existing regular plan holdings into direct plans, nor does it discontinue regular plans.

faq.q: Will I still be able to invest in regular plans?
faq.a: Yes, you can still invest in regular plans. The new SEBI rule only changes the default selection on AMC digital platforms. If you wish to choose a regular plan, you will be informed about its higher expense ratio.

faq.q: What is an expense ratio and why does it matter?
faq.a: The expense ratio is the annual fee charged by a mutual fund to cover its operating and management costs, expressed as a percentage of your investment. It matters because it is deducted from the fund's returns, directly impacting your net gains and overall wealth accumulation over time.

faq.q: Are there any costs involved in switching from a regular to a direct plan?
faq.a: Yes, switching from a regular to a direct plan is treated as a redemption and reinvestment. This can trigger capital gains tax on any profits made from your regular plan units and may also incur an exit load if you redeem before a specified holding period.

faq.q: Who should opt for a direct plan?
faq.a: Direct plans are ideal for investors who are comfortable doing their own research, managing their investments independently, and prefer a cost-efficient approach. Experienced investors who do not require intermediary assistance often benefit most from direct plans.
